contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-twint-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-twint-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-twint-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/accept-a-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/accept-a-payment only lists Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android variants. It establishes no integration prerequisites or payment state transition itself (new raw lines 5-17). The May 3, 2026 guide describes a one-time CHF Checkout Session where the customer approves with an approved TWINT app. The manual Checkout illustrations include card and TWINT, while Stripe also documents dynamic presentation. The legacy Direct API uses a server-created CHF PaymentIntent and client-side confirmTwintPayment with required return_url and optional billing details. Stripe.js handles the redirect. On the separate manual server route, requires_action exposes next_action.redirect_to_url.url. May tests move requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method, and payment status or a webhook is the fulfillment authority (old raw lines 12-106, old raw lines 121-162 and old raw lines 231-357). source-stripe-twint-accept-payment.md preserves the routes but conflates the two redirect behaviors and needs a dated correction.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/accept-a-payment, the November change is navigation-only. The May 3 guide embedded Checkout and legacy Direct API. November links to them and exposes iOS and Android navigation without including variant bodies (old raw lines 8-17 and old raw lines 121-129, new raw lines 9-17). Keep source-stripe-twint-accept-payment.md tied to May's one-time CHF flow, its hosted success_url and embedded return_url examples, its legacy Stripe.js route and its separate server redirect example. The May 3 acceptance table excludes setup and subscription modes from this guide (old raw lines 30-34), while the separate May setup guide illustrates setup mode and the May 13 billing guide illustrates hosted subscription mode with card and TWINT. The November support matrix's three-mode default and unqualified TWINT Checkout row are broader product documentation, and November's separate billing selector gives variant links. Keep those dated scopes and the concept and companion routes reciprocal. Scope the mandate_data examples to future use, since the one-time server example omits it. Preserve server-side verification and webhook fulfillment independently of the browser return. The merchant is told to protect the client secret, while Stripe itself appends it on the configured return (old raw lines 195-224, old raw lines 250-289 and old raw lines 291-357).
